evals.prompt: Design a new module for handling provider notifications — sending emails and in-app alerts when a credential is about to expire. This would be owned by the same team that owns credentialing. We're on a modular monolith in Azure.
evals.expected_output: Architecture proposal with: problem statement, recommendation (stays in the monolith, not a new service), services under Company.App.Api/Services/Notifications/ with an Add<Area>Services() extension, a Storage Queue to an Azure Function for dispatch, a cost line (no new always-on resources), a plain ownership check affirming single-team ownership, and deployment independence. No repository or mediator pattern. No third-party NuGet unless justified.

evals.prompt: Review this architecture: we're building a new Blazor WASM feature for managing user roles. The engineer wants to create a new class library called Company.Portal.RoleManagement.Services to house the service logic separately from the UI project.
evals.expected_output: Assessment that pushes back on the separate class library: server logic belongs in Company.Portal.Api/Services/RoleManagement/, the client's HttpClient service in the Web project's Services/, and shared records in Domain. Concerns section calls out unnecessary project proliferation. Mentions the only valid exceptions: a distributable package, or Core when a second host needs the service.

evals.prompt: I need to add a mapping library to our .NET project for transforming domain models to API response models. The team is used to AutoMapper. Should I use it?
evals.expected_output: Direct recommendation to NOT use AutoMapper: write the projection to a record inside the EF query (or a small static mapping method). Calls out that AutoMapper is a third-party package without a real feature advantage. Notes a license check would be required if a package were used.
